reponse:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Likelihood-shift scores for context use and memory use in retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: We define two scores that need no choice of attention heads or layers. The context score is the gain in log-likelihood of the generated answer when the retrieved documents are present compared with when they are replaced by unrelated documents of matched length. The memory score is the log-likelihood of the same answer under a closed-book prompt relative to the likelihood of a model-free reference answer. Both are read from the output distribution of any white-box model, so they can be computed by a scorer that is not the generator. We evaluate the difference between the memory score and the context score as a hallucination detector on RAGTruth across its question answering, summarization and data-to-text splits, on a post-cutoff news question set we assemble, and with Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as generators and scorers in every combination.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP with its published head and layer selection, SelfCheckGPT, AlignScore, a prompted judge, and raw answer perplexity, all reported with AUROC and precision-recall area; a placebo in which the context score is computed against shuffled documents; detectors fitted on one dataset and tested on the others; three seeds for every sampled quantity.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The difference score should match ReDeEP on the dataset it was tuned on and beat it off-distribution, with AUROC above the prompted judge on question answering. It could fail where summaries paraphrase heavily, since likelihood shifts then track wording rather than grounding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Behavioral reliance scores from counterfactual document edits
PROPOSAL: We measure context use behaviorally rather than through internal activations. For each query we create edited copies of the retrieved documents in which one fact that the answer depends on is replaced by a plausible alternative, using a span-replacement model. The context score of an answer is the probability, estimated under the generator with sampling, that the answer follows the edited fact when the edit is present. The memory score is the probability that the generator reproduces its original claim under a closed-book prompt. An answer whose memory score exceeds its context score is flagged. The procedure needs only sampling access and runs on API models too. We test on RAGTruth and on a fresh news question set with answers dated after the training cutoff of Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe as white-box references on the open models, SelfCheckGPT and a prompted judge as black-box references, a placebo edit that changes a fact the answer does not depend on, and an ablation that scores with a scorer model different from the generator, with bootstrap confidence intervals over queries.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Behavioral scores should reach AUROC within a few points of ReDeEP on RAGTruth and transfer to the news set without any refitting, where ReDeEP degrades. If edits are too easy to detect as out of place, the generator may ignore them regardless of grounding, which would flatten the context score and break the detector.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-agnostic utilisation scores pooled across the whole residual stream
PROPOSAL: Rather than selecting layers, we compute at every layer the cosine similarity between the representation of each generated token and the attention-weighted summary of the context tokens, and the divergence between the representation entering and leaving the feed-forward block, then pool both quantities over layers with a fixed, uniform weighting and over the answer with a maximum. The resulting context score and memory score are therefore defined for any decoder-only model without tuning, and we characterise how much the uniform pooling loses against the tuned selection. We evaluate hallucination detection on RAGTruth and on a long-form summarisation set built from recent news, using Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it, and we optimise nothing on the test datasets.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP with its tuned heads and layers as the reference, the same pooled scores with a random subset of layers, each score alone, raw perplexity as the floor, a prompted judge, and transfer of a threshold fitted on one model to the other two; three seeds on sampled generations and bootstrap intervals on AUROC.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Uniform pooling should lose at most a few points of AUROC against the tuned selection on the tuning dataset and gain on the other datasets and models. The approach could fail if the memory signal is concentrated in a narrow band of layers, in which case uniform pooling would dilute it below the detection threshold.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scoring responses of closed models with a small open proxy scorer
PROPOSAL: Detectors for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) usually assume that the scoring model is the generating model. We test whether a small open-weights proxy can supply the context score and memory score for responses produced by other models, including closed ones served through an application programming interface (API). The proxy computes, for the given response, the log-likelihood gain from the retrieved documents over unrelated documents as the context score, and the closed-book log-likelihood as the memory score, both without any choice of attention heads or layers. Generators are the eight-billion-parameter instruction-tuned Llama 3 model, the seven-billion-parameter Mistral instruct model and two closed chat models; proxies are the same open models plus a one-billion-parameter Qwen 2.5 model. Datasets are RAGTruth and a question answering set on events after every generator's cutoff. The metric is the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
CONTROLS: Same-model scoring where available, which bounds proxy scoring from above; a prompted judge, a sampling-consistency checker and a natural language inference (NLI) verifier that need no internals; proxies of unrelated families to separate family similarity from size; a placebo where the proxy scores a shuffled response; three seeds for all sampled outputs.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Proxy scoring should retain most of the same-model AUROC when the proxy is above one billion parameters, and should beat the sampling-consistency checker on closed generators. It may fail on summarization, where likelihood under a different tokenizer and a different style no longer reflects grounding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Validating utilization scores on documents with planted facts
PROPOSAL: Existing scores are checked only by correlation with hallucination labels, never by whether they track use of the documents. We build a validation suite in which reliance is known by construction. In the first part, the documents contain facts invented for the study, so no model can know them, and a correct answer must come from the documents. In the second part, the documents contradict well-known facts, so a correct answer under the documents reveals context use while the familiar answer reveals memory use. In the third part, the documents are irrelevant and the answer can only come from memory. We score answers from two open-weights instruction-tuned models of seven and seventy billion parameters with likelihood-shift scores that require no layer or head choice, and we ask whether the scores separate the three parts and predict which source each answer followed. We then test the same scores as a hallucination detector on RAGTruth.
CONTROLS: Reimplemented ReDeEP scores on the same suite, raw perplexity and answer length as floors, a prompted judge asked which source the answer used, human annotation of source on a sample of answers, a placebo where documents are shuffled across queries, and bootstrap intervals over queries.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Likelihood-shift scores should classify the source of an answer with accuracy well above the perplexity floor and above the reimplemented ReDeEP scores on the invented-fact part. They may fail on the contradiction part if the models refuse or hedge, producing answers that follow neither source.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Claim-level grounding and recall scores as a black-box utilization detector
PROPOSAL: We decompose each generated answer into atomic claims with a claim splitter, then score every claim twice. The context score of a claim is the entailment probability given the retrieved documents from an off-the-shelf verifier such as MiniCheck. The memory score of a claim is the probability that the generator asserts the same claim when asked the question without documents, estimated from ten closed-book samples with a claim matcher. An answer is scored by the largest gap between memory score and context score over its claims, so no attention head, layer or model internals enter the computation, and the generator may be any model with sampling access. We run the detector on RAGTruth with Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and on a data-to-text split where tables are the documents.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe on the open models, the verifier alone without the memory score, the memory score alone, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge, a placebo that matches closed-book samples to claims from a different answer, and three seeds for the sampled closed-book answers.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The gap score should beat the verifier alone by several AUROC points on question answering, because unsupported claims that the model also states closed-book are the typical hallucination. The detector could fail on data-to-text, where closed-book sampling yields nothing comparable and the memory score collapses to zero for every claim.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Next-token distribution shifts as head-free utilization scores
PROPOSAL: We compare, at every generated position, the next-token distribution of the model given the query and documents with the distribution given the query alone, and with the distribution given the documents alone. The context score of the answer is the sum over positions of the divergence between the full prompt and the query-only prompt, which measures how much the documents move the prediction. The memory score is the sum over positions of the log-probability the query-only prompt assigns to the chosen token, which measures how much the answer was already available without documents. Both quantities are read from the output layer, so no attention head or intermediate layer is selected, and any model that exposes logits can be scored. We evaluate on RAGTruth and on a news summarization set collected after the cutoff of Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP with its published settings, a semantic entropy probe, AlignScore, a prompted judge, each score alone, a placebo computing the divergence against a prompt with shuffled documents, cross-dataset thresholds, and bootstrap intervals over three seeds of sampled answers.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The combined score should match ReDeEP on RAGTruth question answering and transfer better to summarization, where head selection was tuned on a different distribution. We expect failure when answers are long and formulaic, because divergence accumulates on function tokens and swamps the few grounded content tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic entropy under open-book and closed-book sampling as utilization signals
PROPOSAL: We sample ten answers per query under the full prompt and ten under a closed-book prompt, cluster each set by bidirectional entailment, and define the memory score as the probability mass of the closed-book cluster that contains the original answer and the context score as the drop in semantic entropy from the closed-book set to the open-book set. An answer whose memory score is high while the context score is low is flagged as relying on memory. The procedure needs only sampling, so it scores closed models as well as Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and we compare generator-side sampling with sampling from a separate open model acting as a surrogate. Datasets are RAGTruth and a summarization set of recent news articles paired with human labels we collect.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe on the open models, plain semantic entropy of the open-book set without the memory score, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge, a placebo with documents drawn from another query, three seeds for the sampling, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The two-score detector should beat plain semantic entropy on RAGTruth and keep most of its AUROC on closed generators through the surrogate. It may fail on summarization, where clustering by entailment fragments long outputs into many singleton clusters and the entropy estimate becomes noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sentence-dropout regression for a head-free context utilization score
PROPOSAL: We estimate how much each retrieved sentence contributes to an answer by randomly dropping sentences from the documents and regressing the answer log-likelihood on the presence indicators, which yields additive contributions without any choice of attention heads or layers. The context score is the sum of positive contributions, and the memory score is the intercept of the regression, which is the likelihood the model assigns to the answer when nothing from the documents is present. The ratio of memory score to context score is the detector. Scoring runs with the generator or with a different open model, and we test both on RAGTruth and on a question answering set about events after the cutoff of Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe, AlignScore, a prompted judge, a leave-one-sentence-out variant with no regression, each score alone, a placebo where the dropped sentences are replaced by sentences from another document, three seeds for the dropout masks, and bootstrap intervals over queries.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: The regression score should beat the leave-one-out variant and match ReDeEP in-distribution while transferring to the post-cutoff set without refitting. It could fail when the answer is grounded in a single sentence, because dropout then produces nearly binary likelihoods and the regression becomes ill-conditioned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Grounding versus recall scores for detecting hallucinated answers
PROPOSAL: We measure utilization at the level of content units. Named entities, numbers and dates in the answer are extracted and each is labelled as grounded when it appears, after normalization, in the retrieved documents, and as recalled when the generator produces it in closed-book answers to the same query. The context score is the grounded fraction and the memory score the recalled fraction. A trained logistic detector combines the two fractions with their interaction and with answer length. Because the features are extracted from text alone, the detector applies to any generator, including closed models, and never touches attention heads or layers. We train on RAGTruth question answering, and test on the other RAGTruth splits, on a news summarization set collected after the model cutoffs, and on answers from Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and a closed chat model.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP on the open models, AlignScore, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge, the grounded fraction alone, the recalled fraction alone, a label-shuffled placebo for the logistic detector, and three seeds for closed-book sampling.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The combined detector should beat each fraction alone and approach ReDeEP on question answering while staying usable on the closed model. It should fail on abstractive summaries with few extractable units, where both fractions are undefined for many answers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-versus-prior-knowledge likelihood ratio to flag hallucinations in retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: Score each response token by how far its log-probability rises when the retrieved passage is added to the question, and by how much of that log-probability survives when the passage is removed. Combine the two quantities into a response-level ratio through a logistic layer, so that attention heads and layers need not be chosen. Generate answers with Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-2-13B-chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct on RAGTruth, covering question answering, summarisation and data-to-text, then compute the scores with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a model that did not write them. Report area under the ROC curve and F1 per task type on the benchmark's own test partition.
CONTROLS: Compare the ratio against ReDeEP and a token-entropy detector on the same test partition. Compare the ratio against each of its two components used alone on the same partition. Compare a scorer that differs from the generator with a scorer identical to the generator. Compare real passages with passages exchanged between unrelated queries, to check that the external signal tracks the supplied context.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The ratio should reach an area under the curve near 0.80 on question answering and a little lower on summarisation. The claim is refuted when the ratio scores within one point of its better single component, or when scorer mismatch cuts the area by more than 0.1.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual passage scoring of answer reliance in retrieval-augmented generation
PROPOSAL: For every sentence of a response, measure the drop in conditional likelihood when the supplied passage is replaced by an empty string, and the drop when the question is replaced by a generic instruction. Pool sentences with a maximum and give the two pooled numbers to a gradient-boosted classifier, which avoids any choice of attention heads or layers. Collect answers from Gemma-2-9B-it, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on the RAGTruth question-answering and data-to-text subsets, and score them with Mistral-7B-Instruct as an outside model. Give area under the ROC curve, precision at 90 percent recall and F1 for each subset.
CONTROLS: Compare the contrast against a closed-book self-consistency detector and a response-length classifier on the same test partition. Compare the contrast against each of two off-the-shelf sentence-similarity scores used alone on the same partition. Compare a scorer larger than the generator with a scorer smaller than the generator. Compare real passages with passages cut to their first half, to check that the external signal tracks passage length.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should land near 0.78 on question answering and lower on data-to-text. The claim is refuted when the contrast scores within one point of its better pooled number, or when outside-scorer mismatch cuts the area by more than 0.1.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Validating utilization scores by intervening on the retrieved context
PROPOSAL: Build a pair of utilization scores from the shift in next-token distribution, measured by Jensen-Shannon divergence, between the question-plus-passage prompt and the question-only prompt for external use, and between the question-only prompt and a prompt with an unrelated passage for internal use. Validate causally on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with CounterFact-style conflict items placed in a passage: rewrite the passage fact and track external use rising while internal use falls. Then train a small classifier on both scores to detect hallucinations on RAGTruth and the news-summarisation items of FaithBench, reporting area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare responses on passages edited to contradict the model's prior knowledge with responses on unedited passages. Compare the classifier on both scores with the classifier on each score alone. Compare items whose answer the model knows without a passage with items whose answer it does not know. Repeat the validation on a second model family to check that the effect carries across models.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: External use should rise and internal use should fall after a passage edit, with the classifier reaching about 0.78 area under the curve. The test fails if either score moves in the wrong direction after an edit, or if the joint classifier gains under two points over its better single score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy-shift utilization scoring with passage perturbation for hallucination detection
PROPOSAL: Compute external use as the drop in output entropy when the passage is appended, and internal use as the entropy remaining when the passage is replaced by a neutral filler text. Probe the scores on Mistral-7B-Instruct with Wikipedia-derived items in which a date or a name is edited inside the passage, and follow how both scores move after the edit. Fit a decision-tree ensemble on both scores for hallucination detection on RAGTruth and the summarisation part of FaithBench, and report area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare responses on passages edited to change their length with responses on unedited passages. Compare the classifier on both scores with the classifier on the sampling temperature alone. Compare items whose passage opens with a date with items whose passage does not. Repeat the validation at a second decoding temperature to check that the effect carries across temperatures.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Both scores should move after a passage edit, with the classifier reaching about 0.76 area under the curve. The test fails when either score moves in the wrong direction after an edit, or if the joint classifier gains under two points over its better single score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-generator transfer of a context-utilization hallucination detector
PROPOSAL: Train a gradient-boosted detector on utilization features computed by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct over responses written by Llama-2-7B-chat, then test it on responses written by Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B-Instruct and GPT-4 on the RAGTruth question-answering and summarisation subsets. Features are the maximum and the 90th percentile of per-token likelihood gain from the passage and of the likelihood retained without it, so that attention heads and layers need not be selected. Report area under the curve, F1 and calibration error for each generator, plus the Spearman link between each feature and the human span annotations.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out generators with the training generator on the same annotated subsets. Compare the detector with a detector trained directly on each target generator's own responses. Compare passages that fully support the answer with passages that omit part of it. Compare the scorer on answers it wrote with answers written by another model.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should drop by about 0.05 on unseen generators, with the largest drop for GPT-4. The claim fails when the drop passes 0.15 on any generator, or if the transferred detector scores below the in-generator detector by that amount on summarisation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: In-distribution reliability of a utilization-based hallucination detector across question sets
PROPOSAL: Fit a decision-tree ensemble on utilization features computed by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct over responses that Llama-2-7B-chat wrote, then evaluate it on fresh questions answered by that same Llama-2-7B-chat on the RAGTruth question-answering subset and on closed-book TriviaQA answers, with Mistral-7B-Instruct and GPT-4 used only to paraphrase the questions. Features are the maximum and the 90th percentile of per-token likelihood gain from a passage and of the likelihood retained without it, so that attention heads and layers need not be selected. Report area under the curve, F1 and calibration error for each question set, plus the Spearman link between each feature and the human span annotations.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out questions with the training questions from the same generator on the same annotated subsets. Compare the detector with a detector trained on a larger share of that generator's own responses. Compare answers given with a supporting passage with answers given in closed-book mode. Compare the scorer on answers it wrote with answers written by Llama-2-13B-chat.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Area under the curve should drop by about 0.03 on held-out questions, with the largest drop for closed-book answers. The claim fails when the drop passes 0.15 on any question set, or if the closed-book detector scores below the in-subset detector by that amount.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking that utilization scores track real use of context and prior knowledge
PROPOSAL: Construct for each RAGTruth item three prompt variants: the passage intact, the passage with the decisive sentence removed, and the question alone. Define external use as the loss in answer likelihood when the decisive sentence is removed, and internal use as the likelihood kept with the question alone. Validate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct by testing against human span labels marking which response spans come from the passage, then supply both scores to a logistic detector assessed on RAGTruth and the news-summarisation items of FaithBench, reporting area under the curve and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare each score with the human span labels at the span level. Compare scores on spans labelled as copied from the passage with spans labelled as drawn from prior knowledge. Compare detector area under the curve with the area of a detector given only the human span labels. Compare the scores before and after the decisive sentence is removed.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: External use should correlate near 0.5 with copied spans and internal use with prior-knowledge spans. The claim is refuted if either correlation stays under 0.2, or if the detector loses more than 0.05 area under the curve when the scores are replaced by span labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relating utilization scores to the size of the answer and the prompt
PROPOSAL: Take each RAGTruth item in three forms: unchanged, trimmed to its first paragraph, and question only. Define external use as the drop in answer likelihood after trimming, and internal use as the likelihood retained with the question only. Examine Mistral-7B-Instruct on a subset of 500 items, relating both scores to the token counts of the response, then provide both scores to a logistic detector assessed on RAGTruth and the news items of FaithBench, giving area under the curve and F1 for each task type.
CONTROLS: Compare each score with the response length at the response level. Compare scores on responses labelled as long with responses labelled as short. Compare detector area under the curve with the area of a detector given only the response length. Compare the scores before and after the answer is lowercased.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: External use should correlate near 0.5 with response length and internal use with question length. The claim is refuted when either correlation stays under 0.2, or if the detector loses more than 0.05 area under the curve when the scores are replaced by length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory-conflict test of a utilization-based hallucination detector
PROPOSAL: Build conflict items in which the retrieved passage contradicts what the model memorised, using entity swaps on Natural Questions and PopQA passages, plus items where the passage agrees with memory. Compute context use and memory use from likelihood shifts under passage removal on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then train a logistic detector on RAGTruth and evaluate it on the conflict items. Report area under the curve, the fraction of responses that follow memory over the passage, and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare conflict items with agreeing items on the same questions. Compare the detector with a detector that sees response length and passage length only. Compare responses that follow the passage with responses that follow memory, on the conflict items. Compare the two models on the same conflict items.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Memory use should be larger on conflict items than on agreeing items, with the detector reaching about 0.75 area under the curve. A miss shows as memory use that stays level across the two item types, or as a drop below 0.65 area on conflict items.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage-versus-memory scoring on assembled question collections
PROPOSAL: Assemble two collections of items from Natural Questions and PopQA: one in which an entity swap in the passage contradicts memorised facts, and one drawn from unrelated topics with passages that agree with memory. Derive context use and memory use from likelihood shifts under passage removal on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then fit a logistic detector on RAGTruth and evaluate it on both collections. Report area under the curve, the fraction of responses that follow memory over the passage, and F1.
CONTROLS: Compare conflict items with agreeing items on different questions. Compare the detector with a detector that sees response length and question length only. Compare responses that follow the passage with responses that follow memory, on the agreeing items. Compare the two models on different conflict items.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Memory use should be larger on the first collection than on the second, with the detector reaching about 0.75 area under the curve. A miss shows as memory use that stays level across the two collections, or as a drop below 0.65 area on the first collection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Output-distribution shifts as a head-free detector of memory-driven answers
PROPOSAL: We read both utilization signals from the output layer only. At each generated position we compare the next-token distribution under the full prompt with the distribution under the query alone; the summed divergence is the context score, and the summed log-probability the query-only prompt assigns to the chosen tokens is the memory score. An answer is flagged when memory dominates context. Since nothing is selected inside the network, the same code scores Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and any model exposing logits. We evaluate on RAGTruth and on a news summarization set gathered after the cutoffs, and we test whether a threshold set on one dataset transfers to the other.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP, the semantic entropy probe, AlignScore and a prompted judge, perplexity as the floor, each score alone, a placebo using shuffled documents in the full prompt, the planted-fact source test, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The combined score should match ReDeEP on RAGTruth and transfer better to summarization. It fails if divergence accumulates on function tokens, which would make the score track answer length rather than grounding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reranking retrieved documents to lower hallucination in retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: Hallucinations persist even when the documents are relevant, so we test whether tighter retrieval lowers them. We train a cross-encoder reranker on RAGTruth queries with supervision from which document sentences support the labelled answers, and we add a sentence-level filter that keeps only passages scored above a learned cutoff. Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct then answer with the reranked and filtered context. We measure the hallucination rate with the RAGTruth labelling protocol applied by annotators to new answers, on the question answering and summarization splits and on a news summarization set gathered after the cutoffs, and we report answer accuracy alongside hallucination rate to make sure that the filter does not remove needed content.
CONTROLS: The original retriever order, a BM25 reranker, a reranker trained without sentence supervision, filters at three cutoffs, a placebo reranker with shuffled scores, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals over queries.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The sentence-supervised reranker should cut the hallucination rate by a few points without lowering accuracy. It fails if hallucinations are driven by memory rather than by context noise, in which case the rate stays flat across all rerankers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization scores from a model other than the generator
PROPOSAL: We test whether context and memory scores can come from a scorer that did not produce the answer. The scorer computes the log-likelihood gain of the answer from the documents over unrelated documents and the closed-book log-likelihood, both read from the output distribution with no head or layer selection. Generators are Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and a closed chat model; scorers are the three open models and a smaller model of the Qwen family, giving every generator-scorer pair. Datasets are RAGTruth and a post-cutoff question answering set we assemble, and we report AUROC per pair together with the drop relative to same-model scoring.
CONTROLS: Same-model scoring as the ceiling, a scorer given a shuffled answer as the floor, SelfCheckGPT, AlignScore and a prompted judge, scorers from unrelated families against scorers from the same family, the planted-fact source test for every scorer, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Cross-model scoring should keep most of the same-model AUROC when the scorer exceeds one billion parameters, and the smallest scorer should still beat SelfCheckGPT on the closed generator. If scores from unrelated families fall to the floor, the signals are model-specific and the practical claim fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Automated search over heads and layers for stable utilization scores
PROPOSAL: We keep the cosine-similarity context score and the feed-forward divergence memory score, but replace manual selection with a search. For each model we score every attention head on how well its context score separates labelled hallucinations on a development split, and every layer likewise for the memory score, then keep the top-scoring ten heads and three layers under a stability criterion that requires the same choice to emerge from two halves of the development split. Models are Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, each scoring its own answers. Datasets are RAGTruth and a post-cutoff question answering set we assemble, and we report AUROC with the selected heads and layers listed per model.
CONTROLS: The published ReDeEP selection as the reference, random heads and layers as the floor, selection without the stability criterion, selections of five and twenty heads, the planted-fact source test with the selected heads, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals over the development split.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Automated selection should match the published selection on RAGTruth and transfer to the post-cutoff set within a few AUROC points. If selections differ between the two halves of the development split, the signals are not stable and a different model would need its own search.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-book and closed-book sampling entropy as utilization signals
PROPOSAL: We sample ten answers per query with the documents and ten without, cluster each set by bidirectional entailment, and define the memory score as the closed-book cluster mass that contains the original answer and the context score as the entropy drop from the closed-book set to the open-book set. Answers with high memory score and low context score are flagged. Only sampling is needed, so the procedure scores Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as well as a closed chat model, and we compare generator-side sampling with sampling from a separate open model used as a surrogate. Datasets are RAGTruth and a news summarization set with labels we collect.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe on the open models, plain open-book semantic entropy without the memory score, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge, a placebo pairing queries with documents from another query, the planted-fact source test, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The two-score detector should beat plain semantic entropy on RAGTruth and keep most of its AUROC on the closed model through the surrogate. It fails on long summaries if entailment clustering fragments outputs into singletons and entropy turns into noise.

TITLE: Preference fine-tuning toward context-faithful answers in retrieval-augmented generation
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune the generator so that it prefers answers supported by the documents. From RAGTruth we build preference pairs in which the chosen answer is the labelled faithful one and the rejected answer the labelled hallucinated one, and we add synthetic pairs where the rejected answer follows memory against documents that contradict it. We apply direct preference optimization to Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a low-rank adapter, then measure the hallucination rate on held-out RAGTruth splits and on a news summarization set with labels we collect, using the RAGTruth annotation protocol, and we report answer accuracy to check that faithfulness does not come at the price of refusals.
CONTROLS: The untuned models, supervised fine-tuning on the chosen answers only, a placebo adapter trained on shuffled pairs, adapters of two ranks, a system prompt instructing context use with no tuning, the planted-fact source test before and after tuning, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Preference tuning should cut the hallucination rate by several points over the untuned models and over the prompt alone. It fails if the gain comes from shorter, more hedged answers, which the accuracy check would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sentence-dropout contributions as a selection-free context score
PROPOSAL: We randomly drop sentences from the retrieved documents, recompute the answer log-likelihood under each mask, and regress the log-likelihood on sentence presence indicators. The summed positive coefficients form the context score and the intercept, the likelihood with nothing from the documents, forms the memory score; their ratio is the detector. No attention head or layer enters, and scoring can run on the generator or on another open model. We evaluate on RAGTruth and on a question answering set about events after the cutoffs of Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct, and we verify on a planted-fact suite that the coefficients land on the sentences that actually carry the answer.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe, AlignScore, a prompted judge, a leave-one-sentence-out variant without regression, each score alone, a placebo that replaces dropped sentences with sentences from another document, three seeds for the masks, and bootstrap intervals over queries.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: The regression score should beat the leave-one-out variant and match ReDeEP in-distribution while transferring to the post-cutoff set without refitting. It fails when a single sentence grounds the answer, since the likelihoods become nearly binary and the regression ill-conditioned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-reported source attribution as a utilization signal
PROPOSAL: We ask the generator itself how it produced the answer. After generating, the model receives its answer, the query and the documents and is prompted to rate on a five-point scale how much of the answer it drew from the documents and how much from prior knowledge, with a short justification citing the supporting sentences. The two ratings serve as context score and memory score, and an answer is flagged when the prior-knowledge rating exceeds the document rating. The procedure needs no access to internals and no selection of heads or layers, so it runs on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and a closed chat model. We evaluate on RAGTruth and a post-cutoff question answering set, and we check on a planted-fact suite whether the ratings follow the construction.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP and the semantic entropy probe on the open models, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge rating the answer without the two-source framing, ratings from a different model than the generator, three prompt wordings, a placebo rating with the documents replaced, three seeds, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Self-ratings should reach AUROC comparable to a prompted judge and transfer to the closed model unchanged. They fail if models rate document use high whenever documents are present, which the planted-fact suite would show as ratings uncorrelated with the true source.

TITLE: Grounded and recalled content units as a model-agnostic detector
PROPOSAL: We extract named entities, numbers and dates from each answer and label every unit as grounded when it occurs in the documents after normalization and as recalled when the generator produces it in closed-book answers to the same query. The grounded fraction is the context score and the recalled fraction the memory score, and a logistic detector combines them with their interaction and answer length. The features come from text alone, so the detector runs on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and a closed chat model without touching heads or layers. We train on RAGTruth question answering and test on the other splits, on a post-cutoff news summarization set, and on documents that are only partly relevant, which relaxes the usual assumption that retrieval is sufficient.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP on the open models, AlignScore, SelfCheckGPT, a prompted judge, each fraction alone, a label-shuffled placebo for the detector, the planted-fact source test, three seeds for closed-book sampling, and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The combined detector should beat each fraction alone and approach ReDeEP on question answering while staying usable on the closed model and on partly relevant documents. It fails on abstractive summaries with few extractable units, where both fractions are undefined.

TITLE: How document count and position shape hallucination in retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: We characterize when hallucinations occur rather than how they are produced. For every RAGTruth query we vary the number of documents from one to eight and the position of the supporting document from first to last, holding content fixed, and we generate answers with Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and a closed chat model. Annotators apply the RAGTruth protocol to the new answers, and we fit a regression of the hallucination indicator on count, position, document length and answer length, with model as a factor. We extend the design to a post-cutoff news summarization set and to partly relevant documents, and we report the fitted effects with their uncertainty as a map of where retrieval-augmented answers go wrong.
CONTROLS: Shuffled document order as the reference condition, a placebo factor that assigns random positions in the regression, answers with no documents as the floor, three seeds for sampling, and bootstrap intervals over queries for every fitted effect.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The hallucination rate should rise with document count and when the supporting document sits in the middle, with the closed model least affected. The map is uninformative if the effects are smaller than the uncertainty across seeds, which would say that position and count are not what drives hallucination.
